_about: Every input of the Atlas v2 build, pinned (docs/atlas-v2-design.md §2.3 step 0, §2.10a, §7 Phase 0).
fetch-sources.js downloads an entry into src/<id>/ ONLY if its licence is on the accepted list and the
download's sha256 matches; a file that differs from its pin is deleted and the build stops. A source
whose publisher regenerates the file (OSM land polygons, daily) therefore goes stale deliberately:
re-pin it in a commit that says so. Every generated file under atlas/data/ copies the entries it
used into its own header, and the credits page is rendered from those headers.
Licence identifiers accepted: PD, CC0, CC-BY-3.0, CC-BY-4.0 (no conditions beyond credit);
ODbL-1.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, GPL-3.0 (share-alike: only as a data file of its own carrying the licence).
`bytes` is the Content-Length the host reported when the hash was taken; `reachable` records the
probe (node .claude/check-reach.js re-measures it — never trust a date here over a fresh run).

sources.name: ETOPO 2022 Global Relief Model — 60 arc-second surface elevation, ice surface, GeoTIFF (bedrock+bathymetry in one grid)
sources.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information. 2022: ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model. NOAA NCEI. https://doi.org/10.25921/fd45-gt74. Public domain (US Government work).
sources.reachable: 2026-10-08 200 through the agent proxy. The THREDDS fileServer paths (…/thredds/fileServer/global/ETOPO2022/…) answer 404 for the GeoTIFFs; the files live under /mgg/global/relief/ETOPO2022/data/. The 15 arc-second grid is 288 tiles of 15°×15° at …/data/15s/15s_surface_elev_gtif/ETOPO_2022_v1_15s_N<lat>E|W<lon>_surface.tif (e.g. N00E000); the single 60 arc-second file (21600×10800) covers relief levels L0–L2 of §2.3 and is what build-relief.js reads.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap land polygons, complete, WGS84 (osmdata.openstreetmap.de)
sources.version: daily build, planet data of 2026-10-08T00:00:00Z (the README inside the zip names the date; build-land.js copies it into every header) — no versioned URL and no dated archive exist (Zenodo and the Wayback Machine searched 2026-10-08), so the sha256 pins the copy taken that day and a later build will (correctly) fail the pin until re-pinned; the committed atlas/data/ is the citable artefact, reproducible from a re-fetch but not bit-identically
